parts.text:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: The depression group had significantly lower vitamin D levels than healthy controls.
Sentence: "Elevated levels of CRP (p = 0.0038), hs-CRP (p = 0.0048), and IL-6 (p = 0.0030) were identified in the anxiety group, while the depression group was characterized by reduced vitamin D levels (p = 0.0302)."
Measured as: depression group (vs control) vitamin D levels
Population: 50 volunteers: healthy controls and individuals with anxiety, depression or bipolar disorder
Intervention: No intervention; serum vitamin D measured cross-sectionally
Comparator: Healthy control group
Design: case-control study
Sample size: 50
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D levels were not associated with a diagnosis of major depressive disorder.
Sentence: "Vitamin D levels were not associated with diagnoses of major depressive disorder or generalized anxiety disorder."
Measured as: MINI diagnosis of major depressive disorder
Population: Pregnant women from Michigan at risk for depression (by EPDS score or history of depression)
Intervention: Maternal serum vitamin D level (observational, not assigned)
Comparator: Lower vs higher vitamin D levels across participants
Design: cohort study
Sample size: 117
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

{
  "rationale": "Study A compared general volunteers with depression against healthy controls in a case-control design, whereas Study B studied a cohort of pregnant women already at risk for depression.",
  "verdict": "genuine",

  "detail": "population: general volunteers vs pregnant women at risk for depression"
